==English== {{was wotd|2006|June|11}} {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{etymon|en|:bor|frm:cardinal>|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|frm|cardinal}}, from {{der|en|la|cardinālis||pertaining to a hinge, hence applied to that on which something turns or depends, important, principal, chief}}, from ''cardin-'', {{m|la|cardō||hinge}} + {{m|la|-ālis}}, adjectival suffix. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|non-rhotic}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑːd(ɪ)nəl/|[ˈkʰɑːd(ɪ)nəl]|~|[ˈkʰɑːd(ɪ)nl̩]|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑːd(ɪ)nəl/|[ˈkʰɑːd(ɪ)nəl]|~|[ˈkʰɑːd(ɪ)nl̩]|a=AU}} *** {{audio|en|en-au-cardinal.ogg}} * {{a|en|rhotic}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑɹd(ɪ)nəl/|[ˈkʰɑɹd(ɪ)nəl]|~|[ˈkʰɑɹd(ɪ)nl̩]|a=GA,CA}} *** {{audio|en|en-us-cardinal.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhyme|en|ɑː(ɹ)dɪnəl}} * {{hyph|en|car|din|al}} ===Adjective=== {{wikidata lexeme|L30391}} {{en-adj}} # Of fundamental importance; [[crucial]], [[pivotal]]. #: {{co|en|a '''cardinal''' rule}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 8|text=But '''cardinal''' sins, and hollow hearts, I fear ye.}} #* {{RQ:Browne Pseudodoxia Epidemica|edition=2nd|passage=the '''cardinal''' intersections of the zodiack}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=a. 1631|author=w:Michael Drayton|title=To my noble friend Mr. William Brown, of the evil time |passage=Impudence is now a '''cardinal''' virtue.}} # {{lb|en|nautical}} Of or relating to the [[cardinal direction]]s ([[north]], [[south]], [[east]] and [[west]]). #: {{co|en|a '''cardinal''' mark}} # {{lb|en|maths|of a number}} Used to describe quantity (e.g., [[zero]], [[one]], [[two]], [[three]]), as opposed to an [[ordinal]] number indicating relative position. {{gloss|See {{w|Cardinal_number}}.}} # Having a bright [[red]] color (from the color of a Catholic cardinal’s [[cassock]]). # {{lb|en|astrology}} Being one of the signs [[Aries]], [[Cancer]], [[Libra]] and [[Capricorn]], associated with [[initiation]], [[creation]], and [[force]]. #: {{coordinate terms|en|fixed|mutable}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|of fundamental importance}} * Afrikaans: * Breton: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Danish: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * German: * Icelandic: * Interlingua: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kyrgyz: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|гла́вный}}, {{t+|ru|основно́й}}, {{t+|ru|кардина́льный}} * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: * Vietnamese: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|of or relating to the cardinal directions}} * Afrikaans: * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|describing a number that indicates quantity}} * Afrikaans: * Armenian: * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Interlingua: * Italian: * Japanese: * Norman: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|коли́чественный}} * Spanish: * Tagalog: * Turkish: * Vietnamese: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|having a bright red color}} * Bulgarian: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Icelandic: * Irish: * Italian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Vietnamese: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|Aries/Cancer/Libra/Capricorn}} * Finnish: {{trans-bottom}} {{checktrans-top}} * Indonesian: {{t-check|id|Kardinal}} * Irish: {{t-check|ga|cairdinéalach}} {{trans-bottom}} ===Noun=== {{wikidata lexeme|L30392}} {{en-noun|~}} [[Image:Kard Stanisław Dziwisz.jpg|thumb|right|A cardinal (1)]] [[Image:Cardinal side view.JPG|thumb|right|[[northern cardinal]] ({{taxfmt|Cardinalis cardinalis|species}}) (2)]] # {{senseid|en|Q45722}}{{lb|en|Roman Catholic}} One of the officials appointed by the pope in the [[Roman Catholic Church]], ranking only below the [[pope]], equal to the patriarchs, constituting the special college which elects the pope.{{cite-web|author=Press Office|title=The College of Cardinals General Documentazion|titleurl=http://www.vatican.va/news_services/press/documentazione/documents/cardinali_documentazione/cardinali_documentazione_generale_en.html|work=The Holy See|date=17 Feb. 2014|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260812143857/https://www.vatican.va/news_services/press/documentazione/documents/cardinali_documentazione/cardinali_documentazione_generale_en.html|archivedate=12 August 2026}}. #: {{hyper|en|cleric}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1932|author=w:Maurice Baring |chapter=16|title=[http://openlibrary.org/works/OL45537W Friday's Business] |passage=His uncle, a '''Cardinal''', engages a Spanish youth of Moorish descent called Diego, an expert singer and player on the virginal, to unlock the secrets of the heart,{{...}}and cure him by the spell of his music.}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/may/08/white-smoke-signals-election-of-new-roman-catholic-pope|title=White smoke from Sistine Chapel chimney signals election of new pope|date=2025-05-08|author=Angela Giuffrida and Harriet Sherwood|passage=Francis riled conservative '''cardinals''' with his compassion for migrants and refugees, openness towards LGBTQ+ Catholics and demands for action on the climate crisis.
Among the frontrunners before the conclave began were Pietro Parolin, the Vatican’s secretary of state; Luis Antonio Tagle, a reformer from the Philippines; Péter Erdő, a traditionalist from Hungary; Robert Sarah, a '''cardinal''' from Guinea who criticised Francis’s papacy; and the moderate US '''cardinal''' Robert Prevost.|archiveurl=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/Dufgu|archivedate=8 May 2025}} # {{senseid|en|Q223402}} Any of various species of New-World [[passerine]] [[songbird]] in the [[genus]] {{taxfmt|Cardinalis|genus}}, or in the family {{taxfmt|Cardinalidae|family}} more generally, or of similar appearance and once considered to be related to the former; so called because of their red plumage. (See [[w:Cardinalidae|Wikipedia article]] for taxonomical information.) #: {{hypo|en|northern cardinal|red cardinal}} #* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|chapter=Afterglow|page=168|passage=Breezes blowing from beds of iris quickened her breath with their perfume; she saw the tufted lilacs sway in the wind, and the streamers of mauve-tinted wistaria swinging, all a-glisten with golden bees; she saw a crimson '''cardinal''' winging through the foliage, and amorous tanagers flashing like scarlet flames athwart the pines.}} # A deep red color, somewhat less vivid than {{l|en|scarlet}}, the traditional colour of a Catholic cardinal's cassock. {{q|same as {{m|en|cardinal red}}}} #: {{color panel|C41E3A}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1889|magazine=Demorests' Monthly Magazine|volume=25|page=65 |passage=Dark navy-blue, '''cardinal''', golden-brown, old blue, olive, slate-gray, and telegraph-blue are the favorite solid colors seen in heavy beaver cloths {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|math}} {{ellipsis of|en|cardinal number}}, a {{l|en|number}} indicating quantity, or the size of a set (e.g., 0, 1, 2, 3). {{gloss|See {{w|Cardinal_number}}.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1920|author=w:Bertrand Russell|title=Introduction to Mathematical Philosophy|page=83 |passage=This cardinal number is the smallest of the infinite cardinal numbers; it is the one to which Cantor has appropriated the Hebrew aleph with the suffix 0, to distinguish it from larger infinite '''cardinals'''. Thus the name of the smallest of infinite '''cardinals''' is {{m|he||0א}}.}} # {{lb|en|grammar}} {{ellipsis of|en|cardinal numeral}}, a {{l|en|word}} used to represent a cardinal number. #* '''2005''', {{w|Frederic M. Wheelock}}, ''{{w|Wheelock's Latin}}'', 6th ed. revised, p.97: #*: The commonest numerals in Latin, as in English, are the "'''cardinals'''"{{...}}and the "ordinals"{{nb...}}. # {{ellipsis of|en|cardinal flower}} ({{taxlink|Lobelia cardinalis|species}}), a flowering plant. # {{ellipsis of|en|cardinal tetra}} ({{taxlink|Paracheirodon axelrodi|species}}), a [[freshwater]] [[fish]]. # {{lb|en|now|historical}} A woman's short {{l|en|cloak}} with a {{l|en|hood}}, originally made of scarlet cloth. #* {{quote-journal|en|date=1763-08-09|journal=The London Chronicle For the Year 1763|volume=14|page=130|column=2|pageurl=https://hdl.handle.net/2027/mdp.39015080323713?urlappend=%3Bseq=138|text={{...}}; and whilst she was looking over several pieces of each, she took an opportunity of concealing under her '''cardinal''' a piece of cotton, and several handkerchiefs, with which she went off undiscovered;{{nb...}}.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1775|author=w:Richard Brinsley Sheridan|title=The Duenna|section=I.3 |passage=She has valuables of mine; besides, my '''cardinal''' and veil are in her room.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1760|author={{w|Robert Lloyd (poet)|Robert Lloyd}}|title=Chit-Chat, an imitation of Theocritus |passage=Where's your '''cardinal'''! Make haste.}} #* {{RQ:Landon Francesca Carrara|page=274|volume=I|text=Closely drawing her '''cardinal''' round her, she descended into the park, at whose extremity was the little chapel where she intended to make her offering.
